text:
Anya: Heads-up — onboarding gptx-7b-v2 from HF. Chat templates are sometimes getting a leading PAD token in generation, and role markers look shifted. Suspect special-token ID mismatch during HF->Redwood convert.
Sam: Can you paste the tokenizer config / added_tokens snippet?
Anya: Pasting the HF files we got:
```json
// tokenizer_config.json
{
  "bos_token": "<s>",
  "eos_token": "</s>",
  "pad_token": "<pad>"
}

// added_tokens.json
[{"id":100000, "content":"<|role_user|>"}, {"id":100001, "content":"<|role_assistant|>"}]
```
When we run our hf-convert script the mapped IDs differ: `<s>` -> id 1 in HF, but convert output sets `<s>` to id 0 (so PAD ends up as 1).
Mike: Classic off-by-one from re-indexing when merging added_tokens into the base vocab. Our convert flow currently does: load vocab.json, append added_tokens (no remap), then re-generate token->id map. If HF used reserved id slots for special tokens you can end up shifting indices.
Elaine: Also check if the HF tokenizer was using `use_fast = true` and the Rust tokenizer serialized offsets in `tokenizer.json`. We had one model where the fast tokenizer kept special tokens in an internal map (no assigned id) and HF's Python wrapper exposed ids differently.
Sam: Any quick repro command?
Anya: Repro I ran locally: `python tools/convert_hf.py --model-path ./hf/gptx-7b-v2 --out ./redwood/gptx-7b-v2` then `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('redwood/gptx-7b-v2/tokenizer.json'); print(t.token_to_id('<s>'), t.token_to_id('<pad>'))"` -> `0 1` but in HF `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<s>','<pad>'])` -> `1 0`.
convert-bot: Conversion pipeline note: gptx-7b-v2 conversion complete with WARNINGS: duplicated entries in added_tokens.json; fallback remapping applied. See /artifacts/1717432100/convert.log
Mike: Suggested fix: when converting, respect HF-assigned special token ids if present in `tokenizer.json` or `tokenizer_config.json`. Algorithm: 1) parse HF tokenizer.json for special token map; 2) if ids exist and not conflicting, reserve those ids in the new vocab before appending added_tokens; 3) otherwise assign canonical reserved slots (e.g., PAD=0, BOS=1, EOS=2) and emit warning. Also add a reconciliation pass that updates any chat templates referencing token ids.
Anya: I tried a small patch locally: if a special token id exists, we insert a placeholder token at that index before writing vocab. It fixed the chat template repro. Quick diff:
```diff
- vocab_list.extend(added_tokens)
+ # preserve HF special ids: insert placeholders at reserved indices
+ for tok, idx in hf_special_id_map.items():
+     ensure_vocab_has_index(vocab_list, idx, placeholder=tok+'_placeholder')
+ vocab_list.extend(added_tokens)
```
Sam: Nice. Please open a PR with the patch + unit test that converts the toy tokenizer with explicit special ids and asserts token_to_id('<s>') matches HF. Also add a regression eval (small chat prompt) to ensure generation is stable.
Elaine: We should also add a sanity check during ingest that compares token counts and a small signature hash of special-token placements; if mismatch > threshold fail the ingest.
Anya: Will do. I'll open PR in `eng-ml/convert` with tests and link the failing eval diff. For transparency I'll attach the conversion log and a minimal repro script. :thumbsup:
Mike: One more note — quantization paths can expose this silently because q8 kernels may assume PAD=0. Add an assert in the quant runner that pad_id == 0 or explicit mapping exists.
Sam: Agree. Thanks all — looks actionable.
Anya: Thanks — filing PR shortly (will reference ticket #INF-1627).
